author: ohtadmin
title: Robin Foote
text:
Richard “Robin” Foote, 76, of Jamestown, and formerly Quonochontaug, R.I., passed away March 17, 2026, after a brief illness due to complications of a surgery at Adventhealth in Orlando, Fla. He was surrounded by the love and presence of his family.
Robin was born in Windham, Conn., the third of five children to Helen and Dick Foote and grew up in the close-knit “Hill” neighborhood of Willimantic, Conn.
Although he did not live beside the ocean, he traveled every summer to Cape Cod, Mass., and spent time at his grandparents’ Footerest cottage in South Wellfleet. He cherished these visits, where he learned the skill of surf fishing and clamming with his Mim and Pop. While a college student, he returned each summer to work and loved to surf on the big waves at Lecount Hollow beach.
While working as a lifeguard at the Cape Cod National Seashore, he saved the lives of many an inexperienced swimmer from the rip tide and undertow of the furious surf waves for which that area is famous.
He graduated from Windham High School and attended the University of Connecticut School of Business, where he earned a Bachelor of Science degree in business administration and marketing in 1972. Robin began working in his family-owned business, Automatic Business Products/Pharmex of Willimantic. He had several positions in sales, product marketing and strategic planning. He advanced to president and CEO, growing the business to many employees, two locations and increased revenue growth six times.
Robin shared the dream of many to live and raise his family near the beach and ocean. Through great self-motivation of a true entrepreneur, strong work ethic and the creative inspiration of his muse (his wife Maryann), he accomplished this and moved his family from Willimantic to the beautiful seaside village of Quonnie in Charlestown, R.I., where his two sons grew up and enjoyed a wonderful life by the beach and experienced all that coastal living had to offer.
He started his own business, Healthcare Data Corp in Charlestown. HDC began as a provider of electronically published “knowledge bases” or databases in the fields of pharmaceuticals, nutrition, emergency medical treatment and preventative healthcare.
HDC supplied these databases to the nation’s largest drug wholesaler, McKesson Drug Company of San Francisco, and two major drug chains, Super X and People’s. The most innovative product was the MEDILINK technology, which worked with the pharmacy computer using software to generate leaflets and exclusive point-of-care coupons for companion over-the-counter products targeted to the specific prescriptions dispensed to patients.
This electronic coupon program increased over-the-counter sales, provided Laser printers at no cost to the pharmacy and offered a superior patient counseling service. Robin sold his company to Catalina Marketing Services Worldwide in 2000.
Robin was passionate about several things — his love of his family and spending summertime in the salt water ponds and at the Charlestown beaches with his two boys, Colin and Christopher, and his wife, Maryann. All activities with them involved hours exploring Ninigret Pond and Quonnie pond by boat and canoe and exciting exits through the Charlestown Breachway in their boat out into the ocean.
This often meant taking a quick 30-minute cruise to Block Island. Later on, their boating adventures moved to Narragansett Bay in the 25-foot HydroSport, swimming off the boat, fishing, clamming and cruising the bay, especially Mackerel Cove.
Staying active in the winter was important to Robin and his family and many fun ski weekends were enjoyed by the family at Loon Mountain in Lincoln, N.H. and other New England ski areas in Vermont and Maine.
Another interest Robin thoroughly enjoyed was vintage cars, and he was an active car club member. He and his late son, Colin, devoted countless hours restoring two 1970 Datsun 240 Z cars, ultimately earning “Best in Show” awards at multiple venues and later seeing both cars welcomed as part of the Audrain Auto Museum’s collection in Newport, R.I.
Robin loved aviation and this was inspired by his father RW “Dick” Foote, a World War II naval aviator. Around 1975, Robin completed ground school and began flight training at Windham Airport. Logging countless hours in the UConn flying club, he earned his private pilot’s license and began what would become a lifelong journey in the skies.
In 1976, Robin purchased a North American AT-6 Texan from Elmer Ward in Chino, Calif. Freshly rebuilt for competition in the Reno Air Races, the aircraft quickly became a source of pride. His AT-6 was widely regarded as one of the cleanest and fastest on the East Coast — an achievement that earned him the admiration of fellow Warbird enthusiasts.
By 1978, Robin, alongside his father and flight instructor, Tom Rudder, co-founded Warplanes International Airshows. This group of highly skilled pilots showcased a remarkable fleet of World War II warbirds. Robin’s exceptional talent was evident in his precision formation flying and light aerobatics, captivating audiences at airshows throughout the Northeast.
Among his proudest achievements were his first solo flights in two extraordinary aircraft — his father’s Midget Mustang, Lorelei, and a World War II Grumman F4F Wildcat known as Linden Five. Both milestones took place at his home field in Windham, marking defining moments in his aviation journey. Robin’s love of flight endured throughout his life. He owned and flew a variety of aircraft, including a Piper J-3 Cub, a Beechcraft T-34 Mentor and several Light Sport Aircraft. Through every chapter of his life, the sky was not just a passion — it was where he truly belonged.
Robin is survived by his beloved wife, Maryann (Bransford). He was the loving father of Dr. Christopher C. Foote, (Dr. Katie Foote) and the late Colin B. Foote. He was the adored brother of Amy Cerreto, Jackie Clark, Greg Foote and Laurie Roebuck. He was the cherished grampa of William “Liam” Foote and Loretta “Lulu” Foote. Robin also was survived by many nieces, nephews, cousins and a multitude of friends.
He will be deeply missed by all who knew and loved him, but his legacy endures in the lives he touched, the stories he shared and the work he so passionately championed. May his true love of the 1960s and ‘70s music be a blessing and inspiration to all.
Relatives and friends are welcome to join the family at 11 a.m. Saturday June 13, 2026, at a memorial Mass at Saint Mark Church, 60 Narragansett Ave, Jamestown. A “Celebration of Life” reception will follow at JB’s on the Water, 150 Conanicus Ave., Jamestown, from noon to 4 pm.
In lieu of flowers, donations in Robin’s memory may be made to the Beavertail Lighthouse Museum Association in Jamestown or the Warbird Heritage Foundation, 3000 Corporate Drive Waukegan, IL 60087.
Kindly visit www.PatrickQuinnFuneralsandCremations.com for information and online condolences.
